presentingComplaint: Sudden severe central abdominal and back pain with collapse
history: 74-year-old man, lifelong heavy smoker, brought in after abrupt onset of tearing epigastric and lumbar back pain radiating to the left flank while gardening, followed by a brief syncopal episode. Pain is constant and severe. Background of hypertension, treated hyperlipidaemia and peripheral vascular disease. No prior imaging but GP had noted a 'pulsatile tummy' 2 years ago. No haematemesis, dysuria or trauma.
examination: Pale, clammy, cool peripheries and restless. A tender, expansile pulsatile mass is palpable in the epigastrium/periumbilical region with left flank bruising (early Grey-Turner). Peripheral pulses diminished. Abdomen mildly distended, soft elsewhere. No jaundice, no calf tenderness, chest clear, no focal neurology. Pertinent negatives: no urinary symptoms, no radio-femoral delay, no fever.
imaging: Bedside FAST/USS: infrarenal aortic aneurysm ~7.2 cm with surrounding retroperitoneal fluid. CT aortogram (if haemodynamics permit): 7.2 cm infrarenal AAA with active contrast extravasation and left retroperitoneal haematoma confirming rupture.
citations: Harrison 22e - Diseases of the Aorta (aortic aneurysm)
ESVS Management of Abdominal Aorto-iliac Artery Aneurysms 2019
contraindications: Avoid aggressive fluid resuscitation - permissive hypotension (target SBP ~70-90 mmHg / palpable radial pulse) until proximal control
Contrast CT caution with rising creatinine but must not delay definitive imaging/repair
Anticoagulants/antiplatelets worsen haemorrhage - reverse if present
edgeCases: Classic triad (pain + hypotension + pulsatile mass) present in only ~50%; back/flank pain with transient hypotension may mimic renal colic and be missed
Contained retroperitoneal rupture can present deceptively stable before catastrophic free rupture
Aortocaval or aortoenteric fistula variant (high-output failure or massive GI bleed)
expectedMaiK: This is a time-critical vascular catastrophe: a >5.5 cm AAA with hypotension, syncope and a tender pulsatile mass is a ruptured AAA until proven otherwise. Activate the vascular/theatre pathway immediately, use permissive hypotension, and do not delay for extensive workup.
expectedNextQuestions: Is there a known AAA or prior aortic diameter on imaging?
Time of symptom onset and haemodynamic trend?
expectedInvestigations: Urgent CT aortogram (if haemodynamically stable enough)
Bedside ultrasound (FAST) for aortic diameter/free fluid
Group & crossmatch ≥ 6 units with activation of major haemorrhage protocol

investigations: group and crossmatch / major haemorrhage protocol
